[UX] What is your opinion about custom right click context menu in web page?

Personally I'm a bit torn on it. I guess it depends on the underlying interaction model of the webpage. For most webpages I would say that a custom right click menu is more of an annoyance since I tend to open in new tab heavily. On web apps that by design don't use multiple tabs it can work if used sparingly (only on elements where it adds value). In this case I'm really talking about web pages that feel like normal desktop applications with a complicated interaction model (e.g. an online mindmapping app).
Nice point. So it's more to case-per-case basis eh? It is indeed useful in cloud storage like google drive though. On the other hand, it can be bothersome at normal site like voat right?

If you have a website the user will expect a certain experience, a normal right click menu is part of that. If on the other hand you have a web application that's designed to offer the same functionality as a desktop application users expect a context menu.

While there's a spectrum in which web pages and web apps lie, with on one side fully static HTML pages and on the other side applications indistinguishable from desktop ones I would argue that in most cases it's clear what a page is and thus what interaction model can be expected of it.

That doesn't stop web designers with too little UX experience from trying to be fancier than necessary unfortunately.

The only time I see something like that as acceptable is for a full-blown web app, not just any old website. Something like what Mega.nz does is okay, but nothing gets me to stop visiting a website faster than finding out that they're preventing my browser from working properly.
